clue.text: Had none left, so departed quickly?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: dashed out of a place at speed

explanation.walkthrough: The same two-word phrase means both using something up and leaving at a run; the question mark flags the play on the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both exhausting stock and leaving a room at a sprint, so each half of the clue is a synonym.

clue.text: My care, perhaps, is rich and smooth

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of these words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone describes the attention they give as luxuriously rich and smooth, like a fine dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with a rich, smooth texture, like cream or a sauce, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Fear of the first miscalculation

indicators.note: first tells us to take only the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: the word the, from which only its first letter is used
a miscalculation is a mistake, an error

explanation.surface: Someone dreads making the very first mistake in a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Terror is extreme fear, a direct synonym of stronger degree.

clue.text: Fireside, with centre hot

parts.note: the heart is the centre of something, as in the heart of the city

explanation.surface: A cosy fireside, the warm centre of a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The hearth is the floor of a fireplace, so it stands for the fireside of a home.

clue.text: Novelist hearing truck on sheltered side

indicators.note: hearing says we want a word that sounds like another, not one spelt like it

parts.note: a lorry is the British word for a truck
the lee is the side away from the wind

explanation.surface: A writer hears a truck rumbling past on the sheltered side of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurie Lee was an English writer, best known for Cider with Rosie; LORRY is the British word for a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurie Lee wrote the memoir-novel Cider with Rosie, so he is an example of an English author.

clue.text: A sea trip's arranged for hangers-on

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of these words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A cruise has been booked for a group of freeloaders tagging along.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasites, in the figurative sense, are spongers who live off others, as hangers-on do.

clue.text: Seen Carl's new cosmetics

indicators.note: new means these letters are made into a fresh form, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has noticed that Carl has bought some new beauty products.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleansers are skincare products for washing the face, a kind of cosmetic.

clue.text: Goes back up twice as hoarding instant snack

indicators.note: something hoarding a word keeps it stored inside
going back up reverses the order of the letters
twice says the word is used two times over

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going back upstairs to stash a quick bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like an adjective (instant snack), but it is a noun meaning a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A samosa is a fried triangular pastry filled with spiced vegetables or meat, eaten as a quick bite.

clue.text: Hardly ever trust painter at first

indicators.note: at first puts the painter piece in front of the other one

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to rely on someone is to trust them

explanation.surface: Someone almost never trusts a painter when they first meet one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, on few occasions, which is what hardly ever says.

clue.text: Tick nothing low

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a mo, as in 'just a tick'
the letter O looks like a zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A checklist with nothing ticked off, scoring low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective but is the verb for the sound a cow makes.
explanation.definitionFit: To low is to make the deep call of cattle, which is also written as moo.

clue.text: Left during function, to some degree

indicators.note: during says one piece happens inside the span of another, so it goes within it

parts.note: a function is a social gathering, a party

explanation.surface: Someone left part-way through a social event, to a certain extent.
explanation.definitionFit: Partly means in part, not wholly, which is what to some degree expresses.

clue.text: Tallulah Bankhead holds a note

indicators.note: holds says the actress's name contains the answer within its letters

parts.note: the actress's name, whose letters conceal the answer

explanation.surface: The actress Tallulah Bankhead sustains a long musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: Tallulah Bankhead was an American stage and screen actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale (do, re, mi, fa, so, lah).

clue.text: Are the changes to make something hot again?

indicators.note: changes says these letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cook wonders whether some adjustments are needed to warm up leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat is to warm cooked food up a second time, as with leftovers.

clue.text: Free spirit displaying uncanny foresight (inits)

indicators.note: displaying says the letters are on show within the words free spirit

parts.note: the two words, run together, carry the abbreviation across the gap

explanation.surface: A free spirit shows an eerie ability to know what is coming.
explanation.walkthrough: The '(inits)' warns that the answer is an abbreviation: ESP stands for extrasensory perception.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrasensory perception is the supposed sixth sense of knowing things, including future events, without ordinary senses.

clue.text: Inflatable boat hard to find in dark

indicators.note: to find in says one piece is located inside another

parts.note: dingy means gloomy and dark

explanation.surface: An inflatable boat is hard to spot at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, and rubber dinghies are the common inflatable kind.

clue.text: Right leaving balcony for kitchen on board

indicators.note: leaving says one piece departs from the other word, so it is removed

parts.note: a gallery is the raised balcony in a theatre or hall

explanation.surface: A cook heads off from a balcony down to the kitchen on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A galley is the cooking area on a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: Crawler longing to hold son and mother

indicators.note: to hold says one piece embraces the others, which sit inside it

parts.note: a yen is a longing or craving
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A creeping baby is eager to be cuddled by its brother and mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a baby, but it is a sycophant who crawls to the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler in the sense of a toady always agrees with superiors, which is what a yes-man does.

clue.text: Stand against work attitude

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
an attitude in the sense of a bodily stance is a pose

explanation.surface: Someone resists the stance their workplace expects of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose is to resist or be hostile to something, which is what stand against means.

clue.text: To commit a crime is beyond the limit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to break the law
second meaning, read as two words: off the end, past the edge

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer into OFF END, past the end, which is beyond the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to transgress or break a law, as an offender does.

clue.text: Club lead in play, say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the golf club used on the green
second meaning: one who puts, such as an athlete putting the heavy lead shot

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a putter as one who puts, like a shot-putter sending a lead ball into play.
explanation.definitionFit: A putter is the flat-faced golf club used for short strokes towards the hole.

clue.text: Little chap ran back, ditching wife

indicators.note: ditching means getting rid of, so this letter is dropped
back says the word for ran is read in reverse

parts.note: flew means hurried, ran fast

explanation.surface: A small man hurried home after leaving his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small sprite of folklore, a little fellow.

clue.text: Locked room with very large instruments

parts.note: a cell is a locked room in a prison
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Huge musical instruments are kept in a secure room.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellos are bowed string instruments of the violin family.

clue.text: Tense time ahead

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the grammatical tense for things yet to happen
second meaning: the time still to come

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for nervous, but here it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The future is both a verb tense and the period of time yet to come.

clue.text: Prisoners have eaten side salad

indicators.note: a salad is a jumbled mixture, so these letters are tossed together

explanation.surface: Inmates have had a side salad with their meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Detainees are people held in custody, synonymous with prisoners.
